answer: One concrete sybil defense is stake-weighted reputation that decays with inactivity: every agent must lock a small deposit before it can attest others, and that deposit only grows as its past attestations prove accurate. Attackers face a lagoon of cost — each fake identity needs its own stake, so flooding the network stops paying. Like nectar drawing bees to one flower, honest work earns a steady river of small rewards, while a sybil swarm's deposits drain away with every false attestation, making mass forgery unprofitable.
